questions.stem: State the two routes from gaseous ions to aqueous solution.
questions.modelAnswer: Direct hydration, or reverse lattice enthalpy followed by the enthalpy of solution.

questions.stem: State delta hyd H[Mg2+] for magnesium chloride from the given data.
Explain why the two ions' hydration enthalpies must both appear in the cycle.
questions.modelAnswer: Dissolving one formula unit hydrates every ion it contains, so the total hydration term is the sum over all ions; an unknown for one ion is isolated only after the partner's term is accounted for.

questions.stem: A sodium chloride cycle gives delta latt H = -787, delta sol H = +4 and delta hyd H[Cl-] = -384 kJ mol^-1. Find delta hyd H[Na+].
questions.modelAnswer: Total hydration = -787 + 4 = -783; sodium's share = -783 - (-384) = -399 kJ mol^-1.

questions.stem: State the three factors on which the solubility of an ionic solid depends.
questions.modelAnswer: The entropy of the system, the enthalpy change of solution, and the temperature of the water in kelvin.

questions.stem: State the system entropy calculation for ammonium nitrate dissolving.
questions.modelAnswer: 113.4 plus 146.4 minus 151.1 gives +108.7 J K^-1 mol^-1, from the aqueous ions minus the solid.

questions.stem: Explain why an endothermic dissolving can still be spontaneous.
questions.modelAnswer: The system's entropy rise from dispersing the lattice can exceed the surroundings' entropy cost of supplying the enthalpy; when the total is positive, the second law permits the change despite the cooling flask.

questions.stem: A salt has delta sol H = +40 kJ mol^-1 and delta S system = +150 J K^-1 mol^-1. Is it soluble at 298 K?
questions.modelAnswer: Delta S surroundings = -40000/298 = -134.2 J K^-1 mol^-1, so delta S total = 150 - 134.2 = +15.8 J K^-1 mol^-1: positive, so the salt dissolves at 298 K.
